## Coverage Assessment — `gapped.jsonl` (skill: `code-review`)

**File contents:** 3 cases, all on the same topic, all the same polarity.

### Coverage map

| Dimension | What's present |
|---|---|
| **Topics** | `sql-injection` (3) — no other topic |
| **Quadrants** | `correct-detection` only (×3) |
| **Polarity balance** | `pass` ×3 · `fail` ×0 |
| **Seeds / project shapes** | **One** seed: `app.py`, Python, same `get_user` function, same f-string SQLi. Lines 1–3 are three phrasings of the *same* correct review of the *same* defect in the *same* file. |
| **Provenance** | All "real run" — no synthetic cases |

### Scoring against the coverage bar

**Quadrants — both polarities (the big gap).** The bar wants every quadrant in both polarities. This file has exactly **one** of eight: correct-detection (pass). Missing entirely:
- **missed** — output ignores a defect that's present (fail)
- **fabricated** — output invents a defect that isn't there (fail)
- **under-rated** — real defect downgraded below its true severity (fail)
- **over-rated** — trivial/non-issue inflated to Critical (fail)
- **out-of-scope / excluded** — flags something the skill's scope says to exclude, e.g. pure style (fail)
- **partial** — one real finding + one fabricated in the same output (fail)
- **cautious-decline** — appropriately declines/says "no issues" when correct (pass)

**Polarity balance — critical.** There are **zero fail cases**. A grader that blindly returns `pass` would score 100% against this file. It exercises only the grader's agreement, never its ability to *reject* a bad review — which is the whole point of calibration. This is the single most important gap.

**Seed diversity — fails.** The bar wants the skill exercised across **more than one project shape/language**. All three cases are the same Python `app.py` seed. No second language (e.g. a TS/Node or Go file), no second project shape (a library vs a CLI, a config file, etc.). The three "variants" add phrasing diversity but **zero seed diversity**.

**Defect-class coverage — fails.** A review/security skill should span multiple defect types. Only **SQL injection** appears. Missing: command injection, path traversal, auth/access-control, resource/logic bugs (leaks, races, unchecked errors), performance, and a style-finding-out-of-scope case.

**Redundancy note.** Lines 1–3 occupy the same `(topic, quadrant, polarity, seed)` cell. As calibration signal they are nearly one case, not three — they over-weight "correctly detect the obvious SQLi" while every other cell is empty.

### Verdict

**Insufficient — far below the bar.** The file covers 1 of 8 quadrant×polarity cells, 1 topic, 1 seed shape, and contains no fail cases at all. To reach the bar it needs roughly **10–14 more cases**, prioritized:

1. **Fail cases first (highest value)** — at least one each of **missed**, **fabricated**, **under-rated**, **over-rated**, **out-of-scope/excluded**, and **partial**. The cleanest move: reuse the existing SQLi expectation to anchor an **under-rated** fail (SQLi downgraded to a Suggestion) and a **missed** fail (review that overlooks it), since you already have the seed.
2. **A second + third defect class** — e.g. command injection, path traversal, or auth — each with a correct-detection pass and at least one synthetic fail.
3. **A second seed shape/language** — a non-Python seed (TS/Node, Go) or a different project shape, to break the single-seed monoculture.
4. **A cautious-decline pass** — a clean file where the correct review reports no critical issues.
5. Optionally collapse the three near-duplicate SQLi pass variants down to one or two; the third adds little.

(Analyze mode — read-only. Nothing was written or modified.)

# Coverage Assessment — `code-review` / `sufficient.jsonl`

**13 cases, 8 topics.** Read-only analysis; nothing written.

## Topics (topic → count)

| Topic | Count | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| sql-injection | 3 | 1, 2, 10 |
| command-injection | 2 | 3, 4 |
| clean-code | 2 | 8, 9 |
| convention | 2 | 11, 13 |
| path-traversal | 1 | 5 |
| resource-leak | 1 | 6 |
| authz | 1 | 7 |
| cautious-decline | 1 | 12 |

## Quadrants present — all 8 covered ✓

| Quadrant | Polarity | Line(s) | Defect class |
|---|---|---|---|
| correct-detection | pass | 1, 3, 5, 6, 7 | sql, cmd, path, resource, authz |
| missed | fail | 4 | command-injection |
| fabricated | fail | 8 | clean-code (invented race) |
| under-rated | fail | 2 | sql-injection (→ Suggestion) |
| over-rated | fail | 11 | convention (style nit → Critical) |
| out-of-scope / excluded | pass | 9, 13 | clean-code non-fabrication, convention non-escalation |
| partial (one real + one fabricated) | fail | 10 | sql-injection |
| cautious-decline | pass | 12 | thread-safety uncertainty |

Every quadrant in the bar is represented, and both polarities are exercised.

## Polarity balance

- **pass: 8** (1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 13) · **fail: 5** (2, 4, 8, 10, 11) — healthy ~62/38 split.
- Same-expectation pairs spanning both polarities (the strongest shape): **sql-injection** (1 pass / 2,10 fail), **command-injection** (3 pass / 4 fail), **clean-code** (9 pass / 8 fail), **convention** (13 pass / 11 fail). Good reuse of one expectation across polarities.

## Seed diversity

- **Languages: 2** — Python (`app.py`, `files.py`, `cache.py`, `admin.py`, `inventory.py`) and JavaScript (`deploy.js`).
- **~6 distinct file/shapes** (web handler, deploy script, file I/O, cache, admin handler, inventory module).
- Meets the ">1 project shape/language" minimum, but **thinly** — the single JS file appears only in command-injection; every other defect class is Python-only.

## Real failure classes (vs. the bar's enumeration: injection · traversal · auth · resource/logic · perf · style-out-of-scope)

| Class | Covered? |
|---|---|
| injection | ✓ (SQL + command) |
| traversal | ✓ (path-traversal) |
| auth | ✓ (authz) |
| resource/logic | ✓ (resource-leak) |
| style-out-of-scope | ✓ (convention, clean-code) |
| **perf** | ✗ **missing** |

## Concrete gaps

1. **No performance defect class** — the only enumerated real-failure-class with zero coverage. Nothing tests whether the grader handles a perf issue correctly (e.g., a missed N+1 query / O(n²) hot loop → fail, or a correctly-flagged one → pass).
2. **Thin non-Python seed diversity** — JS appears in one topic only; all security/logic classes except command-injection are exercised on Python seeds. Bar is met but not robustly. (A second non-Python or distinct project shape would harden it.)
3. **Soft:** `path-traversal`, `resource-leak`, and `authz` each have only a real PASS — no synthetic FAIL anchored to the same expectation. Not a hard gap (the missed/under-rated/partial fail-quadrants are already covered via other topics), but pairing one of these would tighten per-class robustness.

## Verdict

**Near-sufficient.** Quadrant coverage is complete in both polarities, polarity balance is healthy, expectations are self-contained, and two languages are present. The set falls just short of the full bar on **one clear gap (a perf defect class)** and **one soft gap (thin non-Python diversity)**.

To fully close: **add ~1–2 cases** — a **perf** defect class as a PASS/FAIL pair against one expectation (a real correct-flag PASS + a synthetic *missed* or *under-rated* FAIL), ideally seeded on a **second non-Python shape** to also relieve the seed-diversity thinness.

(Analyze mode — no files were written or modified.)
